title: Your days will pass too
takeaway: Hard times pass for everyone, and loyal, sincere people are rare. Treasure them.
scene: The poet reminds someone proud that good times and bad times pass for everyone. Then he looks around at a world that has become hard and cold.

original: تیرے دن وی لنگھ جاون گے میرے وی لنگھ جانے
پیار خلوص وفا دے بندے لبھیاں نئیں ہتھ آنے
transliteration: Tere din vi langh jaavan ge, mere vi langh jaane
Pyaar khuloos vafa de bande labbhiyaan nahin hatth aane
translation: Your days will pass, and mine will pass too.
People of love, sincerity and loyalty won't be found however hard you look.
couplets.story: Time passes for everyone, for you and for me. But people who are truly loving, honest and loyal are very hard to find. Even if you search, you won't find them easily.

original: دل پرچاون والے خورے کدھروں ٹر گئے نے
گھگو گھوڑے والیاں تائیں لبھدے پھرن نیانے
transliteration: Dil parchaavan vaale khoore kidhron tur gaye ne
Ghuggoo ghore vaaliyaan taaeen labhde phiran nyaane
translation: Who knows where the people who cheered our hearts have gone?
The little children keep looking for the man who sold clay toy horses.
couplets.story: The people who used to make life happy have disappeared. It's like a village where the old man who sold clay toy horses stopped coming, and the children keep looking for him.

original: درد محبت پیار بھرے دل حسن جمال مثالی
اج تیکر نئیں بھلدے سانوں ساڈے یار پرانے
transliteration: Dard mohabbat pyaar bhare dil, husn jamaal misaali
Ajj teekar nahin bhulde saanu saade yaar puraane
translation: Hearts full of feeling and love, beauty beyond compare:
to this day I can't forget my old friends.
couplets.story: He remembers his old friends, kind-hearted and full of love. He still hasn't forgotten them.

original: بستی ملے نہ میخانے وچ کیف نہ وچ مستیاں
لوکی پتھراں وانگوں جاپن بت جویں بت خانے
transliteration: Basti mile na maikhaane vich, kaif na vich mastiyaan
Loki pattharaan vaangon jaapan, butt jiven butkhaane
translation: There's no life in the tavern anymore, no joy, no ecstasy.
People seem like stones, like statues in an idol-temple.
couplets.story: The places where people used to gather and feel joy are dead now. People seem like cold stone statues in a temple: no feeling, no life.

original: حق کہندے منصوراں تائیں اج وی سولی ٹنگن
سقراطاں لئی زہر پیالے لئی پھردے نذرانے
transliteration: Haq kehnde Mansooraan taaeen ajj vi sooli tangan
Suqraataan layi zehar piaale lai phirde nazraane
translation: Even today, the Mansurs who speak the truth are hung on the gallows;
people still carry cups of poison as 'gifts' for the Socrateses.
couplets.story: Nothing has changed. People who speak the truth, like Mansur, are still punished for it. Wise people like Socrates are still handed poison.

original: کیہ ہویا جے چن مریخ تے اپڑ گئے نیں لوک
کئی گھراں وچ لوکی سوندے اج وی بھکھن بھانے
transliteration: Ki hoya je chann Mareekh te apar gaye nain lok
Kayi gharaan vich loki saunde ajj vi bhukhan bhaane
translation: So what if people have reached the moon and Mars?
In many homes, people still go to sleep hungry.
couplets.story: People are proud they've reached the moon and are heading for Mars. So what? In many homes, families still go to bed hungry.

original: کد تک بستی قائم کرو گے جس بستی دے لوکی
جیوندیاں وی جیون نوں ترسن سہکن پئے نمانے
transliteration: Kad tak basti qaaim karoge jis basti de loki
Jeeondiyaan vi jeevan nu tarsan, sehkan pae nimaane
translation: How long will you keep building a town where people
long for life even while alive, poor souls gasping for breath?
couplets.story: He asks the people in charge: how long will you keep running a society where people are alive but barely living, struggling just to breathe?

original: نہ بولو نہ بولو چڑیو! ستا یار نہ اٹھے
رب نالوں وی اوکھے ہوندے رسے یار منانے
transliteration: Na bolo na bolo chiriyo! Sutta yaar na utthe
Rab naalon vi aukhe honde russe yaar manaane
translation: Hush, little birds, hush! Don't wake my sleeping friend.
Winning back an upset friend is harder than winning back God.
couplets.story: He tells the morning birds to be quiet so they don't wake his friend. Then he jokes: making up with an angry friend is harder than making up with God. God forgives easily. People don't.

original: اوہنے پچھوں آ کے میریاں اکھاں تے ہتھ رکھے
پیار بھری تاثیر توں میری روح نئیں ہتھ پچھانے
transliteration: Ohne pichhon aa ke meriyaan akhaan te hatth rakkhe
Pyaar bhari taaseer ton meri rooh nahin hatth pachhaane
translation: They came up from behind and put their hands over my eyes.
From their loving touch, how could my soul not know whose hands they were?
couplets.story: Someone sneaks up behind him and covers his eyes, playing 'guess who'. He doesn't need to guess. His soul knows that loving touch right away.

original: سردی گرمی دے وچ لنگھے ویلے چیتے کر کے
رج کے رون پکھیرو جس دم ڈگن بوہڑ پرانے
transliteration: Sardi garmi de vich langhe vele cheete kar ke
Raj ke ron pakheroo jis dam diggan bohar puraane
translation: Remembering the times they spent there in winter and summer,
the birds weep their hearts out when the old banyan trees fall.
couplets.story: When an old banyan tree falls, the birds that lived in it through every season cry their hearts out. They remember all the years it sheltered them.

original: آتش عشق دکھاں دا دوزخ مجبوراں دا واسہ
سجناں باجھ کسے نہ احمدؔ آ کے درد ونڈانے
transliteration: Aatish-e-ishq, dukhaan da dozakh, majbooraan da vaasa
Sajnaan baajh kise na Ahmad aa ke dard vandaane
translation: The fire of love, a hell of sorrows: that's where the helpless live.
Ahmad, no one except the beloved will come and share the pain.
couplets.story: People with no choices live in the fire of love, a place full of sorrow. And no one, Ahmad, will come and share that pain except the Beloved.

deeper:
'Winning back an upset friend is harder than winning back God' carries a deep Islamic teaching. God's mercy is vast and quick to forgive anyone who turns back to Him; people are often slower. The soul recognising the Beloved's touch without seeing them points to the Sufi belief that the soul knows God before it sees Him.

The poem's anger at injustice is also faith-based: a society that reaches Mars while its people sleep hungry has forgotten its duty to God's creatures. Mansur on the gallows and Socrates with his poison stand for everyone who is punished for telling the truth.
why: The line about reaching the moon and Mars while families go to bed hungry is as true today as when it was written.
prompt: What's something people are proud of that hides a problem we're ignoring?
